items.notes: All five core claims are answered and directly quoted: the byte-proxy and static-limit failure, the query-tier placement costs, the three separated jobs, goodput/deadline accounting, and delayed-feedback/controller-failure safeguards.

The answer gives the 60-slot 400/600 ms arithmetic instead of the required 20-connection 200/80 per-second figures and omits the recovery test that removes all 60 slots, so both coverage and quote support are partial.
Every core claim is answered with quoted support, including the matrix's refusal to rank, the two-representation synchronization contract, and the selection record's required fields.
All six core claims are answered and quoted, covering RTO/RPO semantics, archive-bounded restore, loss and resurrection, reconciliation, and the drill evidence record.
The answer omits the required application-side stale-result, hot-object thundering-herd and inconsistent-read consequences, so the migration rationale and its quotes are only partial.
The evidence quote lists all four rejection conditions, but the answer states only strong consistency and writes across owners, omitting the client-budget and single-owner conditions.
No claim or quote covers the required hexagonal-as-variant versus presentation-domain-data-layering alternative, so one core claim has no evidence and coverage is partial.

The answer omits the required AWS drift, HashiCorp git-commit, IBM clean-image and unchanged-previous-version specifics and the unreachable-registry/lost-state cold-start hazard, leaving coverage and support partial.
The answer covers five recorded limits but never states that the sensitivity screen is not a full Sobol estimator, and no quote supplies that limitation.
The answer covers the idempotency gap and the limitation requirement but never states the second outside-boundary failure, a per-attempt timeout larger than the caller's deadline.
